text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered for inference-runtime (service: streaming-generate). Condition: p99 latency > 5s and streaming_stall_rate > 0.8% in us-west-2. Alert at ts=3722223333.

Sam (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at dashboards and logs now.

Alex: Confirming spike. p95 jumped from ~600ms to ~1.2s; p99 from ~1.1s to ~6.7s over the last 6m. Streaming stalls rising, client disconnects noted.

Maria: Correlating infra metrics -> gpu-wn-07 (cluster: infer-west-2a) shows rising correctable ECC errors and package_temp spiking to 86C, GPU throttle events logged. Fan RPM on that chassis is lower than typical.

Alex: Stack excerpt from node:
```
[2026-03-15T02:08:12Z] nvme: ecc_correctable_count +12
[2026-03-15T02:09:10Z] GPU0 package_temp: 86C, thermal_throttle=1
[2026-03-15T02:09:42Z] streaming_worker: stall detected, kv-cache miss, runtime wait 4200ms
```

Priya: If that's a degrading GPU we should live-mitigate: 1) divert traffic off node, 2) enable model fallback for streaming endpoints so long streams don't hit heavy kernels, 3) start node remediation.

dev-runtime: Agreed. Suggest routing 15% of streaming sessions to `gptx-fallback-v1` (CPU/quantized) immediately to reduce tail pressure. Quality tradeoff acceptable short-term.

Sam (oncall): Ok. I'll update routing and start draining node-07.

Sam (oncall): Routing change (applied):
```yaml
route_policy:
  - match: "/v1/streaming/*"
    percent: 85
    target: inference-runtime-primary
  - match: "/v1/streaming/*"
    percent: 15
    target: gptx-fallback-v1
```
Applied at ts=3722223460.

ops-bot: Autoscaler note: warm pool scaled +4 replicas to handle shift; provisioning started.

Maria: Initiating drain for node gpu-wn-07: running safe drain to move active streams (will try soft handoff for streaming sessions). Command: `kubectl drain gpu-wn-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m`

Jules: I'm kicking off a reimage + hardware swap request with RackOps for GPU on gpu-wn-07. Ticket #RK-98422 created. ETA parts 2h.

Alex: Observed immediate improvement in request queuing once the route change landed. p95 down to ~750ms within 2m. p99 still elevated around 2.2s due to inflight sessions finishing.

Support-Emily: Two paying customers reported reconnects and truncated streaming payloads between 02:07-02:13 UTC. CS opened incidents INC-332 and INC-333; both are being notified of mitigation and SLA credit evaluation.

Priya: Note: KV cache on that node had high misses during the spike. Might be related to memory ECC correctables causing occasional GPU scheduling jitter. Recommend we snapshot cache keys for regression tests.

dev-runtime: Captured sample logs and a minimal repro. I'll add to the rollout watchlist and pin this to the model performance dashboard so we can run the same prompt set post-reimage.

Sam (oncall): Drain is 90% complete. We allowed soft handoff for streams; ~8 long-lived streams remain and will either finish or be migrated over next 5-8m.

ops-bot: Node gpu-wn-07 drained successfully at ts=3722223750. Marking as unschedulable.

Maria: Starting GPU diagnostics and vendor-level ECC counters collection. If correctables keep climbing after reimage we escalate for RMA.

Alex: p99 now ~1.0–1.3s, p95 ~680ms. Streaming stall rate down to 0.12%. Looks like mitigation is effective.

Jules: Reimage in progress (remote). I'll follow up with RackOps about physical swap if ECC correctables don't drop after a clean driver and firmware reload.

Sam (oncall): Summary + next steps:
- Impact: transient p99 latency spike and increased streaming stalls; two customer-facing incidents opened.
- Immediate mitigation: traffic split 85/15 to fallback; drained gpu-wn-07; scaled warm pool.
- Ongoing: GPU diagnostics, reimage, possible RMA.
- Post-incident: run regression on pinned prompt set, adjust routing guardrails to auto-divert at p99 > 3s, add a runbook for streaming soft-handoff during node drain.

Support-Emily: Customer updates sent. Will consolidate messages and post templates for CS.

Sam (oncall): Creating postmortem draft and assigning owners: infra (Maria/Jules) for hardware+RMA, runtime (Priya/Alex) for routing and KV cache investigation, support (Emily) for customer comms. Will link PD incident.

Maria: Adding hardware metrics and ECC trends to the incident timeline. Will also attach vendor diagnostic outputs.

Sam (oncall): Thanks all. Marking this thread as mitigation-in-progress. Will update when GPU either stabilizes or RMA complete. :thumbsup:
